Chubb stock highlights strong underwriting and uneven growth
sum: Chubb Limited's third-quarter results combine record nine-month profitability with uneven premium growth. The company reported the figures for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, in its October 20 earnings release.

Core operating income reached 2.98 billion US dollars in the quarter, or 7.66 US dollars per share. For the first nine months, the measure rose 21 percent to a record 8.60 billion US dollars, while core operating earnings per share increased 24.5 percent to 21.94 US dollars. These are core operating figures, a non-GAAP measure that excludes specified items from net income.

Property and casualty underwriting income fell 8.8 percent year over year to 2.06 billion US dollars, with the combined ratio moving to 84.1 percent from 81.8 percent. Catastrophe losses rose to 705 million US dollars from 285 million US dollars a year earlier, making the reported comparison less favorable despite strong underlying profitability.

Premium trends were mixed. Consolidated net premiums written increased 1.9 percent to 15.14 billion US dollars. North America Commercial premiums declined 2.7 percent, while North America Personal rose 5.3 percent and Overseas General gained 6.7 percent. Life Insurance premiums increased 1.4 percent, and segment income advanced 11.4 percent to 369 million US dollars.

sum: Evan G. Greenberg, Chairman and CEO of Chubb Ltd (NYSE:CB) CB (NYSE:CB) , reported in a Form 4 filed on November 2, 2026, the sale of 13,889 common shares on October 29, 2026, alongside a stock option exercise and an earlier trust account restructuring.
- Share Sale: On October 29, 2026, Greenberg sold 13,889 common shares at a weighted average price of $360.0203 per share, with prices ranging from $360.00 to $360.24.
- Option Exercise: The same day, he exercised options to purchase 719 common shares at an exercise price of $139.01, increasing his direct holdings to 171,347 shares.

- Options Fully Disposed: The 719 options exercised on October 29, 2026, which vested in thirds on February 23 of 2018, 2019, and 2020, were entirely sold, leaving no remaining shares from that option grant.

- Trust Restructuring on May 28, 2026: Previously held 291,163 shares were transferred into a revocable trust with Greenberg as sole trustee and beneficiary, maintaining his pecuniary interest unchanged.

- Post-Transaction Indirect Holdings: After the October 29 sale, the revocable trust holds 277,274 shares; additional indirect holdings include 136 shares held by his wife and 41,564 shares held in his daughter's trust.
- Remaining Stock Options: Greenberg still holds 251,087 options from other grants with varying exercise prices, vesting schedules, and expiration dates, held directly.

Chubb stock weighs record earnings against slower premium growth
sum: Chubb Limited's third-quarter results present investors with a clear contrast: profitability reached a record level, while premium growth remained restrained. The insurer's October 20 release shows that the business is still generating strong returns, but its expansion rate warrants closer attention.

According to the Chubb Corporate Newsroom, third-quarter core operating income rose to 7.66 US dollars per share, while net income reached 7.30 US dollars per share. Consolidated net premiums written increased to 15.1 billion US dollars, up 1.9 percent, with property and casualty premiums and life insurance premiums both contributing to the increase.

The property and casualty combined ratio was 84.1 percent, a level that indicates underwriting remained profitable. Chubb also reported year-to-date core operating income of 21.94 US dollars per share and year-to-date net income of 20.46 US dollars per share. Annualized return on equity stood at 14.5 percent, while core operating return on equity reached 14.6 percent.

For shareholders, the results underline the value of Chubb's diversified insurance platform. Strong underwriting and investment income can support earnings even when premium expansion slows. The trade-off is that a more measured top-line trajectory leaves less room for operational missteps or a deterioration in claims trends.

The next question is whether Chubb can preserve its underwriting discipline while rebuilding stronger premium momentum. A 1.9 percent increase in consolidated net premiums written is positive, but it is materially less dynamic than the growth rates the company has delivered in stronger expansion phases.

That makes the composition of future growth important. Investors are likely to watch commercial insurance pricing, exposure selection and life insurance development alongside the combined ratio. Stable margins would reinforce the earnings case; weaker pricing or higher claims costs would put more pressure on the premium-growth debate.

Can You Invest in State Farm Pre-IPO?
sum: State Farm is the leading auto and homeowners insurance provider in the U.S. In 2023, it held a market share of 18.6% for its auto insurance segment and an 18% market share for homeowners' insurance. The company also provides other types of insurance coverage, such as life, health, and small-business insurance.

In addition to insurance products, State Farm offers several types of investments. To open one, you need to work with a State Farm agent. State Farm investment products include retirement accounts and education savings accounts, like 529 plans, brokerage accounts, and mutual funds. Although State Farm offers investment products, it's not possible to invest in State Farm itself because it is a mutual insurance company owned by its policyholders.
State Farm is not publicly traded on the stock market. Technically, State Farm is a collection of companies, the largest of which is State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Co.

State Farm companies are mutual insurance companies, meaning that policyholders, rather than shareholders, own them. A mutual insurance company's purpose is to provide insurance for policyholders. Any profits are either reinvested in the company or distributed as dividends to shareholders. Other examples of mutual insurance companies include Liberty Mutual, Nationwide, and New York Life Insurance.
State Farm is unlikely to have an initial public offering (IPO) any time soon. It's been a mutual insurance company since its founding in 1922 and has never publicly discussed plans for an IPO.

In the unlikely event that State Farm were to go public via an IPO, it would have to undergo a process called demutualization, in which it would convert from policyholder ownership to shareholder ownership.

Yes, State Farm is profitable overall. State Farm added 130 million new life insurance policies in 2025, which likely contributed to its $12.9 billion net income in 2025, more than double the $5.3 billion net income in 2024 and a stark contrast to the $6.3 billion net loss in 2023.

Chubb's strong underwriting performance, growing investment income and disciplined capital management position the stock for further price appreciation. While its premium valuation may limit multiple expansion, its solid fundamentals should continue to support long-term gains. CB has surpassed earnings estimates in each of the last four quarters, the average being 12.4%.

Shares of some of its peers, like The Travelers Companies, Inc. TRV, have gained 23.6%, whereas W.R. Berkley Corporation WRB and Kinsale Capital Group, Inc. KNSL have lost 3.2% and 31.2%, respectively, in the past year.
